node.title: LEAP: the weighted pair bound is the true envelope for primitive planes
node.statement: Primitive (gcd-trivial, aperiodic) plane counts obey the weighted pair bound: #primitive(P cap D_j) <= C * PairBound(P) with small C — the E7 census sits at ~60% of the floor in both the exact census (38/60) and the kernel sample (13/30). PATH: (1) adopt the packet's PairBound definition; (2) prove it at dim 2 via pencil decomposition through the top concurrency point + the PROVED n/j voting bound; (3) induct via the concurrency form.
node.attack_surface: dim 2 first: a plane is q+1 pencils through any point; the voting bound prices each pencil; the weighting must absorb the overlap — this is where the one new idea lives
node.falsifier: the j=4 Grassmannian refinement (E7's named next step) breaching the envelope
node.notes: CALCULATED LEAP grounded in E7 (PR #183): two independent measurements below floor. If proved at dim 2, F's first open instance closes SHARPLY. | f_dim2_skeleton PROVES the envelope at dim 2 with C = 1 + twin correction — the leap's base case is now route-pinned. | j=4 data point (#183): 28 < 40 — the envelope holds at the second dimension tested; j=4 caveat: active quotient orders 2/4, so structured regression evidence.
